chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Eckstine and Vaughan duets; the Three Varieties with Madeline Green
summary: Budd, Willie Randall and Leroy Harris sing backing as the Three Varieties behind Madeline Green; Budd says Green and Randall had a son.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And what did they -- things there was someplace where they did duos together.
Earl and Sarah?
I mean Billy and -- didn't Billy and --
Oh, yeah. Billy and Sarah did do it. Let's see -- what they did now. Oh, they had several
numbers that they do duets on. Not too many, and of course, you know at that time we had what was called Three Varieties and Madeline Green.
Oh, yes, this stuff and Madeline Green.
See? Madeline Green and Madeline Green was singing with the band, and --
Billy Berty Randall -- saxiphone player. Billy
-- Berty Randall, saxiphone player, Leroy Harris and myself were the Three Varieties.
You sang behind her.
We sang behind her, and we did 'Girl With the Wistful Eyes, It Had to be You, Everything Depends on You, that's another Charlie Carpenter number. He wrote that number.
Right.
And we had some pretty good hits. We sound very good. In fact, I've listened to some of those things recently, and I'm amazed at the harmony we were singing and, you know, how great it sounds.
That's most interesting because you used to write for the -- backgrounds for singers. This is first time I remember singers singing background to singing.
That's right. And Jerry Valentine and myself, we did most of -- all of that work. And --
Uh-huh. Tell me a little bit about Madeline Green. She was very -- was she married to Willy Randall at one time?
She was not married to Willy, but she -- you might say --
(Unintelligible).
-- they were common law, AND MARRIED LATER
(Simultaneous remarks)
They had a son even.
Is that so? (YES THEY HAVE A SON)

Yeah. They were heavy roomers, and you might say common law, and actually right today Willy goes to Cleveland, and his son has made some pretty good strides, I think, and he was in the Army, his son, and everything, and Willy still is crazy about that boy. And he goes and see her, and I haven't seen Madeline for a long time.
